about: Golden set for the receipt reader, built from real photographed receipts.
WHY IT EXISTS (2026-09-03): the reader was handed raw file bytes, and Claude
never receives image metadata, so a receipt lying sideways on a table was
read sideways — and answered CONFIDENTLY WRONG. IMG_4047 is a Hornbach
receipt for 496,80 kr; raw, the reader called it 'ICA, 841,85 kr' at
confidence 0.72, and 'ICA, 524,90' on the next run. A wrong number that
looks certain walks straight through review, which is what makes this worse
than a failure. IMG_4058 is the same file that produced the unexplained
'Byggmax 2 948 kr' beside a Hornbach photo in session 89.

The images are private receipts and are NOT in the repo. Point the runner at
Ground truth below was read off the images by hand, not produced by a model —
a check derived from the same source as the data inherits the source's errors.
Grow this set as new failure shapes appear; five cases is a floor, not a goal.

cases.note: Reference case. Raw read invents an ICA receipt with a different total on every run.
Total 2208,00 is the receipt sum; 1983,00 is only the card leg (225 came off a gift card). Reading the card leg as the total is a real failure mode.
One article bought in 8 units. 'Summa [8]' is the unit count, not the row count — reading it as 8 rows is the trap.
Raw read called this Hennes & Mauritz.
Session 89's unexplained 'Byggmax 2 948'. Two VAT rates (25 % on goods, 12 % on the energy drink), so the 25 %-check alone cannot catch a misread here.
